You can buy Korean skincare online from a mix of Korea-based retailers (big selection, often best pricing) and US-based/authorized stores (faster shipping, easier returns, lower counterfeit risk). Here are solid options:

## Korea-based retailers (huge selection)
- **Olive Young Global** (official Korean drugstore chain; lots of sets and promos)
- **YesStyle** (large catalog; check “ships within” times since some items are stocked later)
- **StyleKorean** (frequent sales; good for bundles)
- **Jolse** (often good prices; periodic free-shipping promos)
- **Stylevana** (good prices but shipping can be slow depending on stock status)

## US-based / authorized retailers (faster, easier returns)
- **Soko Glam** (curated; strong educational content)
- **Peach & Lily** (curated; good for starter routines)
- **Ulta** and **Sephora** (carry select K-beauty brands; easy returns)
- **Amazon**: only if you buy from the **brand’s official storefront** or clearly listed **authorized sellers** (avoid “too good to be true” pricing)

## Buy direct from brand sites (best for authenticity)
If you already know the brand you want (e.g., COSRX, Beauty of Joseon, Laneige, Innisfree, et al.), buying from the **official brand website** or official marketplace store is usually the safest.

## Quick safety checks (to avoid fakes)
- Prefer **official retailers** or **brand-authorized** sellers.
- Be cautious with deep discounts on marketplaces.
- Check **seller name**, **return policy**, and **recent reviews** (with photos).

If you tell me your budget, skin type (oily/dry/sensitive/acne-prone), and what you want to target (acne, pigmentation, anti-aging, barrier repair), I can recommend which store + a few product picks that are easy to find there.
